name: Western Big Game Migration and Connectivity Fund
summary: Funds from the Bureau of Land Management, passed through the Foundation, for fencing changes, winter-range habitat restoration and water projects that help pronghorn, mule deer and elk on BLM-managed sagebrush lands.

geography.label: BLM-managed lands in the western US

eligibility.rule: Address pronghorn, mule deer, or elk needs identified in a State Action Plan
Be located in state-identified priority areas, sagebrush habitat, and on BLM-managed lands and waters
For multijurisdictional projects, matching contributions cover all non-BLM components

documents: Letters of support or acknowledgement from the State Fish and Wildlife agency and BLM field or district office

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include state government agencies, non-profit 501(c) organizations, local governments, municipal governments, tribal governments and organizations.

geography.quote: The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) manages millions of acres of priority big game habitats throughout the West

access.quote: Applications must be submitted in the Foundation's grant portal.

amount.quote: Award sizes will range but requests should not exceed $250,000.

co_finance_required.quote: Projects are expected to provide a 25% non-federal cost-share ($0.25 of matching contributions for every $1 requested).

eligibility.quote: All applicants must be registered in SAM.gov.
Projects may benefit multiple species but must specifically address needs for pronghorn, mule deer, or elk as identified in a State Action Plan.

All projects must be located (1) within state-identified priority areas as identified under SO3362, (2) in sagebrush habitat (core sagebrush habitats preferred: Core Sagebrush Areas map - PDF; ScienceBase - Shapefile), and (3) on BLM-managed lands and waters.
Projects can be multijurisdictional if matching contributions cover all components of the project which are not located on BLM-managed lands and waters.

documents.quote: Applications must include a letter of support or acknowledgement from both the relevant State Fish and Wildlife agency (Director preferred) and the relevant field or district office of the BLM.

co_finance.quote: Projects are expected to provide a 25% non-federal cost-share ($0.25 of matching contributions for every $1 requested).
